claims.statement: The pinned chat precedence fragment ranks personal instructions above repository instructions above organization instructions, while all relevant sets are still provided. Priority is not exclusion of lower-priority context or guaranteed resolution of every conflict; this source does not override the current operating contract.

The conflict fragment recommends avoiding contradictory instructions and proposes temporary repository-instruction disablement for response-quality concerns. Its link targets code-review settings despite generic wording; applicability must not be generalized silently and no toggle was changed.

The effective-instruction fragment recommends concise self-contained broadly applicable repository context because instructions accompany chat messages, including purpose, coding conventions and tools/framework versions. These are starting-point recommendations, not a universal format or adherence certificate.

The full example describes a task web application's stack, coding preferences and interface style. These are illustrative choices, not this repository's adopted stack or instructions executed by this reviewer.

The guidance qualifies external-resource demands, answer style and rigid detail limits as potentially problematic in large diverse repositories even if workable in small teams. Its negative examples demonstrate possible ineffective instructions, not mandatory communication rules.

The code-review toggle fragment says custom instructions default enabled and repository settings enable/disable them for every review in that repository. Navigation includes were inspected, but UI presence, permissions and effective review behavior were not verified.

The chat toggle fragment says default-enabled repository instructions can be disabled/re-enabled for the user's own chat use without affecting others. This personal scope is distinct from repository-wide code-review changes.

The further-reading fragment links conceptual/configuration material and community customization examples. Reference links do not mark upstream pages reviewed or vetted, grant reuse rights or adopt their instructions.
